db_evidence.notes: Clue interval 1 (28394-28645) is fully present in event_steps/event_chains but is internally ambiguous: the boss fight's own victory screen literally reads '得胜'/'已击败 妖王·九尾灵君' (defeated Nine-Tailed Spirit Lord), while the immediately following post-boss cutscene shows a name banner reading '亢金星君' (Kangjin Star Lord) next to the same red-robed woman, revealing her true identity per Journey-to-the-West lore. The reference answer expects the revealed true name, not the literal victory-screen boss name, and the DB rows for this window return in a duplicated/non-strictly-chronological order across three overlapping event_chains, making it easy to anchor on the wrong name. Clue interval 2 (37535-37576) -- the actual martialist duel that should be visually checked for the worn armor -- is present in topic_facts/event_steps only as generic combat description ('character in wide-brimmed straw hat', 'leopard-patterned clothing', cavern boss fight with fire effects); no row anywhere in the DB contains the literal string '翠笠武师', so locating this exact duel requires either semantic/visual matching or lucky proximity search, and none of the 5 rollouts ran clip_qa on this exact window.

root_causes: The question's key entity (翠笠武师, Green-Capped Martialist) never appears verbatim anywhere in the memory DB text, forcing every rollout to guess the correct duel window from vague visual descriptions or semantic search; the 5 rollouts landed on 5 different candidate windows (66180-66270, 69570-70140, no window/28xxx only, no window/28xxx only, 54960-55080), only one of which is even close to correct, and none matched the dataset's true clue_interval-2 (37535-37576).

For the boss-identity clue (interval 1), the DB itself carries two plausible boss names for the same fight -- the literal victory-screen name (妖王·九尾灵君) and a separately-named entity revealed in the immediately following cutscene (亢金星君) -- and 3 of 5 rollouts anchored on the more salient/literal victory-screen text rather than the cutscene's revealed true identity that the reference answer wants.

Rollout 0 scored 5 despite verifying the wrong duel window (66180-66270 instead of 37535-37576) and naming a different boss (亢金龙, a separate 'kang jinlong boss trial' fought at 23430s) than the reference's 亢金星君 -- it happened to reach a name close enough in English gloss ('Kangjin') to satisfy the judge, which suggests judge leniency on transliteration rather than a fully correct retrieval chain.
None of the 5 rollouts ran clip_qa on the actual 37535-37576 window that the dataset marks as clue evidence for the martialist duel itself.
what_worked: Rollout 0's strategy of first visually pinning down the specific armor name via clip_qa, then searching topic_facts/event_steps for when that armor became forge-able, is a sound general approach and got it to the right neighborhood in time (28650s, adjacent to the true clue_interval-1) even though the initial duel window it chose for the clip_qa was wrong.

All rollouts correctly ruled out the '翠笠武师' literal-text search path early (0 SQL rows), and instead pivoted to semantic_search / broad time-window run_sql, which is the correct fallback when a named entity is absent from the DB.
transferable_lessons: When a question names a specific enemy/character that returns zero literal-text SQL hits, treat this as a signal to run clip_qa on multiple time-window candidates (not just one) before committing to an armor/name identification, since a single wrong window silently propagates into a wrong final answer.

When retrieved rows around a boss-defeat show two different names for what appears to be the same character (a victory-screen name vs. a post-fight cutscene name-banner), prefer the name that a following cutscene explicitly reveals as the character's 'true identity', especially in games with disguise/reveal tropes -- do not default to the most literal/on-screen 'defeated X' text without checking for a subsequent identity reveal.

Be alert to duplicate/overlapping rows returned for the same time window from multiple event_chains; do not assume SQL result order reflects true chronology -- sort/verify against start_s explicitly and check for cutscene-vs-combat interleaving before picking evidence.

When the dataset provides no way to know the true clue_interval in advance, cross-check any visually-identified duel window against ALL available textual descriptors (hat/headwear, clothing pattern, weapon, terrain) mentioned in the question before running clip_qa, since generic gameplay windows in this DB recur many times with superficially similar descriptions (multiple boss/duel scenes with hats, cloaks, fire effects, snow terrain).
open_questions: Is 亢金龙 (kang jinlong, the separate boss fought at 23430s) and 亢金星君 (the cutscene-revealed identity at 28170-28530s) meant to be understood as the same in-game entity/star-lord under the game's Journey-to-the-West lore, or are they genuinely distinct bosses that happen to share the 'Kangjin/亢金' name prefix? This determines whether rollout 0's score of 5 reflects a correct underlying answer or a judge scoring the transliteration loosely.

Whether the judge's rubric for this question checks the boss's canonical/revealed name specifically (亢金星君) or would also accept the literal victory-screen name (妖王·九尾灵君) under different phrasing -- rollouts 2 and 3 gave essentially the DB's most literal answer and were scored 0, suggesting the reference is strict about the revealed identity, but this was not independently confirmed against a judge transcript.
